applicable_when: The kernel is severely underutilized: Compute SM at 14.69% and only 13.4% achieved occupancy. The root cause is 128 registers/thread, which caps occupancy at 4 blocks/SM (25% theoretical). The scheduler is starved — 78.58% of cycles have no eligible warp, with 57.6% of stalls from MIO/shared-memory operations (13.1-way bank conflicts). The kernel currently sets ALLOW_TF32=False, forcing FP32 FFMA on the tl.dot accumulation. Enabling TF32 (allow_tf32=True) allows the GPU to use Tensor Cores (MMA instructions) instead of FFMA. Tensor Core MMA instructions have ~8x higher throughput than FP32 FFMA, and critically they use shared memory differently — the MMA warp-level instructions use warp-cooperative shared memory access patterns that are inherently conflict-free, which directly addresses the 13.1-way bank conflict penalty. For this workload (M=36000, N=24, K=96), the K dimension is only 96, so accumulated TF32 rounding error (mantissa reduced from 23 to 10 bits) over 96 K-steps is well within acceptable tolerance (atol=1e-3 is easily met for K<=512). The diversity instruction explicitly targets this optimization.

The diversity instruction mandates TMA loads: replacing scalar pointer arithmetic with tl.make_tensor_descriptor + tl.load on Hopper offloads address generation to the dedicated TMA hardware unit, enables asynchronous bulk copies via async pipelines, and eliminates the strided scalar loads that cause the bank conflicts. Combining TMA with @triton.autotune to explore smaller BLOCK_M (reducing register pressure) and num_stages (software pipelining) will compound the benefit.

applicable_when: The kernel uses BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=32 with 128 threads. Each thread owns a 1x32 row of the 128x32 accumulator. When threads load from shared memory for the dot product, they access elements with a stride of 32 elements (BLOCK_N), causing 13.1-way bank conflicts because 32-element strides map multiple threads to the same bank. The 128 registers/thread (maximum) limits the SM to only 4 blocks, yielding 0.53 waves/SM and 13.4% occupancy. Reducing BLOCK_M (e.g., to 64) and increasing BLOCK_N (e.g., to 64) would: (1) halve the accumulator rows per thread, reducing register usage; (2) change the shared memory access stride to avoid bank conflicts; (3) double the grid size to ~564 CTAs, improving SM utilization. Adding @triton.autotune explores the full configuration space automatically.
